messages:
Noah Kim: Hey folks, quick onboarding benefits/payroll q's from week 1. I filled out the Workday stuff but want to confirm: when does my medical/dental/vision coverage actually start? Also need to submit a $120 travel expense for my trip to HQ for orientation — what's the best way? And finally, my offer mentioned biweekly payroll but didn't say cutoff dates. Thanks!

Ethan Cole (People Ops): welcome Noah! :wave: Short answers: 1) Coverage effective date = first day of the month following 30 days after your start date (typical). So if you started 2024-05-10, coverage usually starts 2024-06-01. 2) Travel expense: submit via Spendesk and tag "onboarding". For mileage or personal car use attach a map and mileage calc. 3) Payroll cutoff: we close payroll on Tuesday 11:59pm PT for the Friday pay run. If you miss cutoff, you'll be paid the next cycle.

Noah Kim: Got it — I started 2024-05-10. So coverage would be 06/01. If I have a dentist appointment on 05/25, it's not covered, correct? Any way to get an exception?

Ethan Cole: Correct, routine appointments before effective date are not covered. Exceptions only for emergency/urgent care and need case review with the carrier. If you want us to open a case, DM me the clinic + date and I'll escalate.

Noah Kim: Thanks. About dependents: I need to add my partner to benefits, do I do that in the same Workday enrollment flow or is there a separate form?

Lina Patel (Payroll): Add dependents in the benefits enrollment portal (Workday -> Benefits). You'll need SSN/DOB for each dependent and a domestic partner affidavit if not married. Deadline is 30 days from start to get them on the plan without a qualifying life event.

Noah Kim: Cool. Spendesk URL? I couldn't find it in the handbook. Also any receipts I should definitely keep?

Finance-bot: Spendesk: https://tools.redwood/spendesk Submit receipts as PDF or photos. Required attachments: itemized receipt, proof of payment (card or bank), and brief business purpose (eg "HQ orientation 05/12 - travel"). Travel over $250 requires manager pre-approval.

Noah Kim: My travel receipt is $120 — uploading now. One more payroll detail: I set up direct deposit but didn't realize there are alternate deposit options. Is paper check an option?

Lina Patel: Paper check is available but slower and we encourage direct deposit. If you prefer check, set your payment elections in Workday and confirm with payroll@redwood. Note: international hires have different routing for cross-border transfers.

Priya Nair (Manager): tagging to confirm I approve the onboarding travel expense. Priya here — approved. :white_check_mark: Noah, welcome to the team! If you need the Spendesk tag changed to "eng-onboarding", let me know.

Noah Kim: Thanks Priya! Submitting with "onboarding" tag now. Any guidance on PTO/holidays during probation? My offer mentioned some pro-rating.

Ethan Cole: PTO accrues from day 1 but usage may be limited by the 90-day policy in the handbook (managers can approve earlier on a case-by-case basis). Company-fixed holidays are pro-rated based on start date for the first year. If you have a specific day off request, request in Workday and Priya can approve.

Noah Kim: Understood. Final question: if I buy a small desk lamp (~$45) for the home office, is that reimbursable or should I request it from IT?

Priya Nair: For small desk items <$75, reimburse via Spendesk and tag me as approver. For monitors/keyboards please coordinate with IT first.

Noah Kim: Perfect. Thanks everyone — sending Spendesk request and double-checking Workday entries. Appreciate the quick help! :blush:
